svg.title: Tuning KP, from above
svg.desc: An animation, seen from above, of the same line-following program run three times on a taped circle, with a different KP each time. The robot follows the outside edge of the tape with its left sensor, driving clockwise, and a blue line traces its path. With KP = 0.2 the correction is too small for the curve: the robot drifts outward and leaves the line. With KP = 0.5 it holds the edge with small corrections. With KP = 1.0 it over-corrects, swerving back and forth across the edge. Beside it, the three lines of the loop, and a box showing the left reading, the error and the correction as the robot drives.
svg.text: the outside edge of the tape
The same loop, three KP values
Nothing changes between the three runs
but one number. Too low and the robot
can't steer hard enough for the curve;
too high and every small error turns
into a big swerve past the edge.

g.text: too gentle: it drifts off the line
the right KP holds the edge
